html:
The Story of the Weeping Camel is a 2003 film by the Mongolian director Byambasuren Davaa and the Italian Luigi Falorni, made as a student project at the film school in Munich. It follows a family of herders in the Gobi Desert of southern Mongolia in spring, when a mother camel rejects her rare white calf after a hard birth.

The family tries everything, then sends two boys across the desert to a town to fetch a musician. In an old ritual called hoos, a woman sings to the camel while the musician plays the morin khuur, the horsehead fiddle, until the camel weeps and lets the calf suckle. The film is a docudrama: the family and the ritual are real, but the scenes were arranged for the camera. The boys' trip to town also shows television arriving in the herders' lives.

It was nominated for the Academy Award for best documentary and found a wide audience abroad. It shows the life of herders of the Bactrian camel going on after the end of communism, much as it had for centuries.
